title: Poireaux Vinaigrette
subtitle: Warm leeks dressed with sharp mustard vinaigrette
excerpt: Leeks simmered until silk-tender then dressed while still warm with a sharp Dijon vinaigrette. A French bistro staple that works as a starter or a side.
sourceNotes: Classic French bistro dish. Leeks are traditionally served warm so the vinaigrette soaks in.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook the leeks up to 2 hours ahead. Dress them just before serving.

content.text: Leeks cooked until just tender absorb vinaigrette beautifully. Dress them warm so the flavour goes all the way through. Do not overcook them or they turn slimy.

items.prepNote: trimmed, white and pale green parts only

content.text: Bring a large pan of salted water to a boil. Add the leeks in a single layer if possible.
Cook for 12 to 15 minutes until a knife slides through the thickest part with no resistance.
Lift the leeks carefully into a colander. Leave to drain for 5 minutes. Do not rinse them.
Whisk the mustard and vinegar together in a small bowl. Whisk in the oil in a slow stream until combined. Stir in the shallot, salt, and pepper.
Arrange the warm leeks on a serving plate. Spoon the vinaigrette over them generously.
Leave for 10 minutes so the dressing soaks in. Scatter over the parsley before serving.

items.symptom: The leeks are slimy in the centre.
items.fix: Cook until just tender and drain immediately. Check at 12 minutes with a knife tip.

items.symptom: The vinaigrette splits and looks oily.
items.cause: The oil was poured in too fast.
items.fix: Pour the oil in a thin stream while whisking constantly. A dab more mustard also helps keep it together.

items.cause: The dressing went on too late when the leeks had cooled.
items.fix: Dress while the leeks are still warm. The heat helps the vinaigrette penetrate.
